epics.title: Legacy repo upgrade
epics.objective: Carry a repo vendored before the factory/ rename onto the current harness in one command, leaving no stale copy of the gate surface and no story that can no longer be closed

tasks.title: forge upgrade retires the legacy .agents/ tree and reports what survives
tasks.objective: Detect a pre-rename target, carry its skill-evolution state and client-added skills out of .agents/skills/ into factory/skills/, retire the old tree only when every file left in it has a counterpart in the newly vendored factory/, and report the project-owned files that still name .agents/ without editing any of them.
acceptance_criteria: upgrading a repo carrying .agents/ leaves no .agents/ tree and a complete factory/ tree
skill-evolution dirs (proposed, rejected) and client-added skills under .agents/skills/ survive at factory/skills/
a path under .agents/ with no counterpart in the vendored factory/ tree aborts the upgrade, is named, and nothing under it is deleted
the output names every project-owned file still referencing .agents/, excluding archived evidence under .factory/history/
no project-owned file is modified by the migration
upgrading a repo already on factory/ behaves exactly as before
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "upgrade or adopt"
tasks.reviewer_focus: the retire step must run AFTER preserved skills are restored, or their .agents/ originals look unrecognized and abort a clean upgrade. The report must read tracked files only (the real target carries node_modules/) and must write nothing.

tasks.title: stage migrate records an explicit base commit
tasks.objective: forge stage migrate takes --base <sha>, validates that it resolves and is an ancestor of HEAD, and stamps it as base_sha on every legacy stage it adopts, so a story that was open when its repo was upgraded can still be measured and closed.
acceptance_criteria: stage migrate without --base refuses and names the flag
process identity is whitespace-normalized at every source, so observed processes are still recognized as live on single-digit days of the month
a discovery failure degrades discovery only; already-known processes still run the full SIGTERM to SIGKILL escalation
a base that does not resolve to a commit is refused
a base that is not an ancestor of HEAD is refused
the resolved sha lands as base_sha on every adopted active or done stage, alongside the task_sha256 the command already stamps
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "migrate or stage_done or reaps or termination_signal or process_identity"
tasks.reviewer_focus: --base is required with no default; conduct 5 forbids a compatibility shim for a once-per-repo command whose only consumer is its own test. dirty_at_start stays unset on purpose - _measure defaults it to {} and a commit base makes that the honest baseline. The delegate.py identity normalization is the inherited defect that blocked this stage's own verify: check both identity sources collapse whitespace the same way.
